title: Acme Retail onboarding eval kit
summary: Working eval pack for onboarding Acme Retail: generator and product-metadata enrichment use cases. Includes pinned prompt suite, private dataset references, concrete acceptance criteria for quality/latency/regression, and an initial sign-off checklist. This is a living doc; expect iterations after first round of human review.
customer: Acme Retail (B2C e-commerce; catalog size ~1.2M SKUs)
use_cases: Generate SEO-friendly short product descriptions (<= 280 chars) from structured specs
Enrich category-level metadata (attributes mapping, normalized size/fit text)
Detect and redact PII when merchant-supplied fields contain owner/contact info
private_datasets: acme_catalog_2024_q2_sample.csv (internal id: ds-acme-024) — 5k rows sampled across top 10 categories; includes title, specs, merchant_description, category_id
acme_human_refs_product_descriptions.csv (id: ds-acme-ref-11) — 2k human-written short descriptions used as gold references
merchant_raw_attribute_dump_2024.jsonl (id: ds-acme-attr-7) — noisy attribute text for normalization tests
acme_pii-needleset.csv (id: ds-acme-pii-3) — curated list of merchant-owned test emails/phones to validate redaction
evaluation_metrics: Quality: human-preference rate vs. baseline generator >= 55% (pairwise A/B with blind reviewers)
Hallucination: factual error rate <= 2% on product spec facts (measured against spec fields)
Attribute normalization: token-level F1 >= 0.88 on canonical mapping testset
PII redaction: recall >= 0.98 and precision >= 0.95 on needleset
Latency: p50 generation end-to-end <= 250ms; p95 <= 700ms (hosted API), measured on 16-token output baseline
Token cost: per-output-token cost should not increase > 10% vs. current model baseline when using recommended quantization profile
acceptance_criteria: Pass automated unit tests (format checks) for pinned prompts against sample inputs
Achieve evaluation_metrics thresholds on held-out eval split (see private_datasets)
No high-severity hallucination cases in 500 random human-reviewed outputs (severity defined in severity_matrix sheet)
PII redaction tests show no false negatives on needleset; any false-positive patterns must be documented and approved
Performance SLOs satisfied under 95th percentile traffic simulation with Redwood Dedicated staging cluster
Security checklist: dataset access audited, KMS keys used for private datasets, and ingestion logs retained per Acme policy
regression_test_plan: Run nightly regression against the saved eval snapshot (eval_snapshot/acme_2024-09-18). Steps: 1) Run full eval harness (quality + metrics) on staging dedicated instance. 2) Run 1000-sample human review job for edge-case tagging. 3) If any metric drops > 3% relative to baseline, trigger rollback and open JIRA-MLONB-REG regression ticket. Use metric-level tolerances defined in CONFLUENCE-1203. Maintain historical metric CSVs in s3://redwood-evals/acme/ for trend analysis.
rollout_and_monitoring: Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours -> 25% for 72 hours -> 100% if stable. Monitor: human-preference sampling every 6 hours, token-level cost per route, hallucination alerts (automated heuristics + manual triage), and PII-detection counters. Configure automatic fallback to previous model variant on increased hallucination alert rate (> 5 incidents/hour) or latency SLO breach (>10% of requests over p95 threshold). Dashboard links: CONSOLE-DASHBOARD-ACME-GEN (internal).
notes_and_open_questions: Merchant-supplied spec fields sometimes contain HTML blobs — should we run a normalization pre-step or rely on prompt-level cleaning? (action: Jin to prototype pre-normalizer)
Edge case: bundles with >10 items — how to summarize succinctly within 280 chars? Consider special prompt path for bundles.
Acme asks for brand voice variants (formal / playful). Current eval focuses on default neutral voice; need separate prompt matrix for voice A/B tests.
Data retention: Acme requested 30-day retention for sampled inference traces; confirm with security if this complies with company policy vs. customer contract
